My opinion is that allowed multiboxing is sanctioned cheating, and any game that allows it is selling its principles for money.
I’m all for getting every possible advantage inside a game, but once you step outside the actual game and start abusing the account/client system for in-game advantage, the line gets blurry.
At that point, why stop there? If using extra clients to gain power is acceptable just because the company monetizes it, then that just opens the door to ANY kind of cheating, including hacking.

Change my mind.

To me, it's fine, it's meant to be balanced around one person's ability to control said characters, if there is no input broadcasting, I don't mind it. If someone is using 3rd party tools to broadcast inputs across multiple accounts then they are cheating.

If you're manually tabbing to each account and manually pressing every hotkey I see no problem with it.

In the earlier years when the game was sub only, you were allowed to use input broadcasting, at least the ToS didn't explicitly forbid it.

As far as I'm concerned, boxing adds to the failures, quite often people lose titans because they were looking at other characters. Just adds to the complacency.
Sure. I don't personally care if other players multibox. Multiboxing is not something you need to do in order to be successful in EVE and whether they ban it or not, my world simply would not change.

You know... you still need to send manual commands on every active alt you are using. Macros or boting orders are a baneable ofense.

Is not that simple like hit F1 on all screens and have an instant or eventual win in a fight.
Thats not how fights (maybe ganks) works. I like to see marauders PVP on youtube and this ones are tanking monsters who can beat whole fleets alone and actually win if agresors are not micromanaging every alt.

Even for mining the game make sound alerts but you still need to micromanage every screen and figure out where the alert is coming is not easy or fun at all.

Every MMO has multiboxing with the exception of Albion Online and it isn't going anywhere soon.

It doesn't really matter what you or anyone else thinks about it. It will continue as a practice so long as it makes the developers money.
